title: Revise contrast token deprecation plan and redesign keyboard focus zones for dense components
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: During the last round of VPAT prep we surfaced a set of inconsistencies across our color token ramp and the way focus outlines are applied in dense components (compact tables, action lists, and sparkline/mini charts). Several partner teams reported that focus rings are visually clipped at small row heights and that chart updates are not announced reliably to screen readers. Goal: produce a minimal-compatibility plan that (1) stabilizes a contrast token subset for compliance and deprecation, (2) reworks keyboard focus zones so focus never visually clips in compact densities, and (3) add ARIA patterns / live-region guidance for small charts and table row updates. Deliverables include token mapping docs, updated component specs, a VPAT addendum, and handoff-ready tickets for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Contrast token subset defined and documented with WCAG AA/AAA mappings for normal and compact densities
Component specs updated: tables, action lists, buttons, and mini-charts include explicit focus visuals that do not clip at compact heights
ARIA and live-region guidance documented for chart updates and table row live announcements
VPAT addendum drafted and reviewed by Security and Accessibility SME
Engineering tickets created with visual regression test checklist and QA acceptance steps
tasks: Run color contrast scan across current token set and export failing combos
Design candidate token subset for deprecation and replacement mapping
Prototype focus ring variants for 32px, 28px, and 24px row heights in Figma
Workshop keyboard nav behavior with Eng (focus order, virtualized lists, and scroll-into-view)
Define ARIA live-region patterns for sparkline updates and row-level updates
Draft VPAT addendum mapping affected components and remediation status
Create ENG tickets with acceptance test vectors and screenshots
Coordinate QA test matrix including macOS VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, iOS VoiceOver
comments: 2025-02-18 | Ava Patel: Kickoff — consolidated reports from QA and partners. Noted two priority pain points: focus clipping at 24px rows and missing live-region for chart datapoint updates.
2025-02-21 | Jonah Rivera: First pass Figma prototypes added (three focus ring thicknesses). Raised question about token renaming strategy to avoid breaking existing CSS variables.
2025-02-25 | Accessibility SME (Maya Chen): Confirmed that AA is sufficient for many surfaces but recommended AAA for small UI text in dense tables; flagged three token pairs as non-compliant.

2025-02-28 | Jonah Rivera: Workshop with ENG (SRE and Runtime teams) — agreed on using an accessibility utility that toggles a 2px inset focus outline for compact rows and fallbacks for legacy browsers.
2025-03-03 | Ava Patel: Draft VPAT addendum uploaded to Confluence for security review. Created ENG tickets ENG-4127 and ENG-4128 for implementation and visual regression tests.
2025-03-04 | Jonah Rivera: Design review scheduled for 2025-03-06 with PM and Accessibility SME; updated acceptance criteria to include voiceover test pairs.
review_feedback: PM (Rita Gomez): Ensure impact on existing product theming is documented and include migration notes for customers who use raw tokens.
Engineering (Kyle Park): Prefer minimal DOM changes — suggested CSS-only solution for focus visuals where possible; requested explicit test vectors for virtualization edge cases.
Accessibility SME (Maya Chen): Add explicit guidance for aria-live politeness levels and when to use role=alert vs aria-live=polite for chart updates.
notes: Risk: token deprecation may cause downstream teams to see visual regressions; include a migration guide and codemod where feasible
Opportunity: standardizing a compact focus utility reduces repeated engineering work across teams
Suggested follow-up: schedule a customer-facing changelog and migration webinar if we change public tokens
